items.title: U.S. bans foreign-made humanoid robots, targeting China over national security - NBC News
items.summary: # U.S. bans foreign-made humanoid robots, targeting China over national security. The FCC said the advanced robots produced in foreign countries pose supply chain vulnerabilities to the U.S. as well as cybersecurity and national security risks. HONG KONG — The Federal Communications Commission in the U.S. said it would ban the import of foreign-made humanoid robots in a move that targets China, arguing they pose a national security risk. China makes substantially more humanoid robots than the U.S. and other competitors, and analysts estimate that Chinese humanoid robots’ global market share has reached roughly 85%. In making the decision, the FCC said these advanced robots produced in foreign countries pose supply chain vulnerabilities to the U.S. as well as cybersecurity and national security risks. When it comes to global markets, China is also targeting Europe, for example, as a key market for its advanced robots including humanoids, Omdia said.

items.title: Alif Holding Plans 'Made in UAE' Production in Abu Dhabi - Stock Titan
items.summary: 4. Robo.ai and Abu Dhabi Enterprise Jointly Establish AI Industrial Group Alif Holding to Serve Infrastructure, Government and Industrial Sectors. **Robo.ai (NASDAQ: AIIO)** announced a joint venture with Abu Dhabi-based Eleven International Holdings to establish **Alif Holding**, an intelligent industrial technology group headquartered in Abu Dhabi. The Group will develop intelligent software and smart equipment for government, infrastructure and industrial sectors across the UAE, GCC and global markets. Alif Holding is built around two platforms: an intelligent equipment platform focused on robotics, automation, advanced composite materials and manufacturing, and an intelligent software platform covering industrial AI, computer vision, AI agents and large language models, digital twins, and data and analytics. According to Robo.ai, the initiative aligns with the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and Abu Dhabi’s ambition in advanced industry, while PwC estimates AI could add close to **US$96 billion**, or about **13.6%** of GDP, to the UAE economy by 2030.

items.title: Naperville Central teen takes 2nd in international art contest - Chicago Tribune
items.summary: Naperville Sun |   Naperville Central teen takes 2nd in…. # Naperville Central teen takes 2nd in international art contest. Naperville Central High School student Claire Shen placed second in the 15- to 18-year-old age group of the 2026 Young Artists and Authors Showcase. The international competition invites the submission of original works of art, writing, photography, film and music to express the Sister Cities International mission. Shen’s work titled “Through the Looking Glass” was entered in the showcase’s Classic Art category. It was inspired by a train ride from Naperville to Chicago, she said. “Watching the neighborhoods transition into the city’s skyline, I began to see the journey as a metaphor for change, growth and the unknown future,” Shen said. I titled the piece, ‘Through the Looking Glass,’ because the train window serves as a portal between the familiar and the unknown.”. Michelle Mullins is a freelance reporter for the Naperville Sun.
